memoryReview.evidence: covers/fog-of-conquest.jpg (inspected legacy cover, capture commit unknown)
memoryReview.lesson: The geographic field and geographic orders belong to FOG; retain this source game’s specific object rather than copying its map presentation.

memoryReview.evidence: covers/zamazka.jpg (inspected legacy cover, capture commit unknown)
memoryReview.lesson: Painted restoration and the paper illustration are its central objects; this port keeps its recovered source art and its own playable control topology.

references.observation: The source page places its Diplomacy map and simultaneous-order rules beside supply-center explanations.
references.principle: Make the public board explain the consequences of privately selected orders.
references.application: Keep public faction state visible while each opponent seals a private political choice.
references.avoid: Do not import territory movement or Diplomacy’s negotiation rules into this duel.

references.observation: The official hosted game page introduces a two-player civilization duel through its shared card and victory systems.
references.principle: A duel needs a legible shared consequence for each individual card choice.
references.application: Keep the revealed round and persistent victory counters together on the political board.
references.avoid: Do not copy another game’s card artwork, symbols or three victory rules.

references.observation: The publisher presents distinct illustrated woodland factions and an asymmetric struggle on one common board.
references.principle: Give factions recognizable identities while retaining a common public state.
references.application: Preserve the source faction colors and court illustrations as the stable political vocabulary.
references.avoid: Do not reproduce Root characters, woodland setting or asymmetric faction rules.

concepts.medium: The original DOM board, card renderer and local authored artwork make individual rules readable without canvas text scaling.
concepts.composition: The shared royal board is followed by the current laws and a hand of selectable illustrated decree cards.
concepts.interaction: Select an illustrated decree from your own hand, seal it, then read the combined law and shared board consequence.
concepts.motion: A selected card is marked immediately; after both choices the round advances and the new public state persists.
concepts.rationale: Chosen for this restoration because the user requested the existing project and its recovered rules, content and recognizable scene.

concepts.medium: A new WebGL miniature with raised physical pieces and a freely orbiting camera instead of the recovered scene renderer.
concepts.composition: An oblique miniature sits in a circular tabletop with controls represented by surrounding physical tools.
concepts.interaction: Orbit the miniature, inspect an object and manipulate it through projected three-dimensional handles.
concepts.motion: Camera inertia, object weight and spring settling would replace the source input timing and discrete presentation.
concepts.rationale: A future reinterpretation could make the object tactile, but would rebuild the renderer and make precise phone input less direct.

concepts.medium: An illustrated DOM folio with static authored state panels and short textual outcome cards.
concepts.composition: A sequence of full-screen spreads isolates one choice and one outcome at a time, with no permanently visible playfield.
concepts.interaction: Turn from a choice spread to a result spread and inspect a chronological illustrated history.
concepts.motion: Page folds and a deliberate pause between choice and result would carry the rhythm of the interaction.
concepts.rationale: A separate narrative version could explain rules slowly, but would conceal the continuously shared state needed by this recovered game.

selection.reason: The requested work is restoration and integration of an existing game. Retaining its actual playable object, rules and recovered content serves that request with the least loss of identity.

rejected.reason: A new orbiting renderer would replace rather than restore the source presentation, introduce new assets and make the present direct controls less predictable.
A sequence of isolated spreads would hide simultaneous state and continuous interaction that define the source game’s playable loop.

tools.reason: The recovered browser renderer runs in local Chromium; app-local SVG install artwork is authored as editable vector geometry.

assets.role: Authored app-specific install identity accompanies the retained playable scene and appears in the page and PWA manifest.
assets.acceptance: Its concrete game motif remains distinguishable at small icon scale, without the temporary Forge monogram.
assets.integration: The PWA manifest and page icon load the local exported SVG without a CDN or network image dependency.
assets.provenance: App-specific SVG geometry authored for this restoration. Existing playable artwork remains the recovered user project content.

risks: Phone controls may obscure the playable object; review full-viewport captures after real input, not only canvas crops.
An online state update must not restart entry animations or conceal the resulting board or world state.
comparisons: FOG geographic playfield versus this source game object at phone scale.
ZAMAZKA restoration controls versus this source game input and feedback loop.
